analysis.title: UBS Cash Trading - Main Themes 28th October
key_insights: US equities trade sideways after the European close (S&P +60bps, Nasdaq +1.2%), with SOX and memory names leading +3-3.5%. EStoxx started -30bps.
KOSPI is up about 7%, on track for its best day in three months, after SK Hynix's Q3 print and a capital return of about 100tn won (~$45bn). SK Hynix shares +10%, Samsung +8%.

TAIEX +2% on news of OpenAI and Oracle partnerships with Google, supporting chip supply chain names (MediaTek +7%, TSMC +1%). TSMC is reported to be lifting advanced packaging prices by 20% on AI demand.

Crude is up 1.5-2% (WTI $101.5, Brent $115.8) after a WSJ report that the US told several Gulf states to prepare for a short, intense military campaign after the midterms. This puts escalation risk back on a dated horizon.
The desk expects Tech/Nasdaq/AI to grind higher as sentiment recovers on earnings delivery. GOOG and MSFT results after the close today are described as pivotal.

UBS base case for tonight's FOMC is a hold, likely by a 10-2 vote, with Warsh keeping a hawkish message that there is still 'more work to do' on inflation. UBS expects 25bp hikes in both December and January.
Markets price about a 10% chance of an October hike, 92% for a 25bp December hike and 33bps of cumulative hikes by January.

UBS Economics expects a cautious UK Autumn Budget. Fiscal headroom may have fallen from £23.6bn in March to about £10bn, and the Chancellor is expected to rebuild a buffer of roughly £15bn through smaller tax increases while deferring tougher decisions to 2027.

UBS sees maintaining the UK fiscal rules as supportive for gilts, GBP as relatively resilient into 2027, and selective equity opportunities in housebuilders, property, lower-value consumer names and public-investment beneficiaries rather than a broad UK equity rerating.
A UK bank windfall tax is under discussion. Verbal consensus has the bank levy moving toward 8% from 3%. UBS modelled 3% to 6%, implying a 3-4% cut to NWG/LLOY numbers and 1-2% for BARC/HSBC.

European cash equity flow on Tuesday was better to buy (54/46), with participation about 30% above the YTD run rate. Technology was the busiest sector (16% of turnover) and balanced. Industrials (14%) were better bid, and Banks (14%) saw demand in French and UK names.

market_movers.rationale: SK Hynix shares rose 10% after a strong Q3 print and a capital return of about 100tn won (~$45bn). SK Hynix has no direct US listing identified in the report.
Samsung shares rose 8% alongside the memory move after SK Hynix's results.
TSMC is reported to be lifting advanced packaging prices by 20% on AI demand, and shares rose 1%.
GOOG results after the close today are described as pivotal for tech sentiment. OpenAI and Oracle partnerships with Google were reported.
MSFT results after the close today are described as pivotal for tech sentiment.
UK banks NWG, LLOY, BARC and HSBC face a possible bank levy increase. UBS models a 3-4% cut to NWG/LLOY numbers and 1-2% for BARC/HSBC at a 6% levy.

sector_views.rationale: SOX and memory led US trading by 3-3.5% on the SK Hynix print, the TSMC packaging price increase and AI demand.

sector_views.sector: UK housebuilders, property, lower-value consumer, public-investment beneficiaries
sector_views.rationale: UBS Economics sees selective opportunities from the cautious UK Budget, rather than a broad UK equity rerating.
A bank levy increase from 3% toward 8% is under discussion. UBS models 3% to 6%, cutting earnings estimates 1-4%.

earnings_insights: SK Hynix Q3 reported a blowout print, with a capital return of about 100tn won (~$45bn). Shares +10%. The report gives no EPS figure.
GOOG and MSFT report after the close on 10/28. No estimates are given.
European earnings are heavy today, ahead of the UK Budget and the FOMC.

macro_indicators.interpretation: UBS base case. Warsh is expected to stay hawkish, saying there is 'more work to do' on inflation.
UBS expects two further hikes with no strong forward guidance. Markets price 92% for December and 33bps cumulative by January.
Markets largely agree with UBS that the Fed holds in October.
Sticky inflation rather than accelerating inflation, which reduces urgency to hike immediately.
Expected buffer rebuild of about £15bn via smaller tax increases.

trade_ideas.description: Selective long UK housebuilders, property, lower-value consumer names and public-investment beneficiaries around the UK Autumn Budget
trade_ideas.rationale: Maintaining the fiscal rules should support gilts and GBP, and the Budget offers selective equity opportunities rather than a broad rerating.

risk_factors: Escalation risk in the Gulf on a dated horizon after the US midterms.
Sticky US inflation around 3% with further Fed hikes expected.
A UK bank levy rising toward 8% from 3%.
A tighter UK fiscal position, with headroom down to about £10bn.
GOOG and MSFT earnings could disappoint after the tech rally.
vol_and_positioning: Market sensitivity to the geopolitical headlines is seemingly lower on a day-to-day volatility basis.
Flow on Tuesday was 54/46 better to buy, with participation about 30% above the HT YTD run rate.

Technology was 16% of turnover and finished balanced, with two-way flow in Semis. Industrials were 14% and better bid, with demand across Electricals, A&D and Maintenance. Banks were 14%, with selective positioning in UK names ahead of the Budget.
Healthcare and Energy saw demand. Telecoms, Food & Bev, Utilities and Insurance saw supply.
geopolitical: WSJ reported the US told several Gulf states to prepare for a short, intense military campaign after the midterms, putting escalation risk on a dated horizon.
US midterm elections are cited as a reason for the Fed pause.
A UK bank windfall tax is under discussion ahead of the Autumn Budget.
